P.title: P.blurb
Corporate AI: Bringing AI into a company: use cases, architecture, governance and value.

P.title: corp-why.summary
Corporate AI: The value levers behind the hype.

P.title: corp-why.q0.q
Corporate AI: Which is NOT one of the four main AI value levers?

P.title: corp-why.q0.x
Corporate AI: The levers are productivity, decisions, customer experience, new revenue.

P.title: corp-why.q1.q
Corporate AI: Why do many AI pilots fail to reach production?

P.title: corp-why.q1.o1
Corporate AI: Data, integration, process change and trust aren't addressed

P.title: corp-why.q1.x
Corporate AI: The model is rarely the main blocker.

P.title: corp-why.q2.q
Corporate AI: A good AI project starts from…

P.title: corp-why.q2.o1
Corporate AI: A business problem with an owner and measurable outcome

P.title: corp-why.c0.text
Corporate AI: AI creates business value in four main ways: doing work faster and cheaper, making better decisions, improving customer experience, and enabling new products or revenue.

P.title: corp-why.c1.text
Corporate AI: Automating or accelerating routine knowledge work, such as reading documents, drafting, reconciling, answering standard questions, frees people for higher-value work.

P.title: corp-why.c2.text
Corporate AI: Forecasting demand, prices, risk or maintenance needs more accurately reduces waste and improves margins. In trading, small forecast improvements can be worth a lot.

P.title: corp-why.c3.text
Corporate AI: Faster, 24/7 answers, personalised recommendations and quicker processing of orders and claims improve satisfaction and loyalty.

P.title: corp-why.c4.text
Corporate AI: AI can screen transactions for fraud, check contracts against policies, monitor sanctions lists and flag anomalies far faster than manual review.

P.title: corp-why.c5.text
Corporate AI: The strongest AI programmes treat AI as a capability for growth and better work, not just headcount reduction. Framing affects adoption: people embrace tools that help them.

P.title: corp-why.c6.text
Corporate AI: Value tends to concentrate in core processes with high volume, repetitive judgement and lots of documents or data: finance operations, customer service, supply chain, sales and software development.

P.title: corp-why.c7.text
Corporate AI: Many pilots never reach production. The gap is usually not the model but data, integration, process change and trust. Plan for those from day one.

P.title: corp-why.c8.text
Corporate AI: As competitors adopt AI, the baseline for speed and cost shifts. Waiting can mean falling behind; rushing without foundations can waste money. A steady, prioritised approach wins.

P.title: corp-why.c9.text
Corporate AI: The best AI projects start from a business problem with an owner and a measurable outcome, not from a technology looking for a use.

P.title: corp-why.c9.viz.items.0.r
Corporate AI: we need to cut invoice processing time by half

P.title: corp-usecases.summary
Corporate AI: Spotting and prioritising where AI helps.

P.title: corp-usecases.q0.q
Corporate AI: Which ideas should usually go first?

P.title: corp-usecases.q1.q
Corporate AI: AI deciding on job applicants is which risk tier?

P.title: corp-usecases.q1.x
Corporate AI: Decisions about people are high risk.

P.title: corp-usecases.q2.q
Corporate AI: Forecasting demand is best suited to…

P.title: corp-usecases.q2.x
Corporate AI: Numbers and history suit predictive models.

P.title: corp-usecases.c0.text
Corporate AI: Good candidates involve repetitive tasks, lots of text or documents, clear rules with many exceptions, or decisions based on historical data.

P.title: corp-usecases.c1.title
Corporate AI: Ask the people who do the work

P.title: corp-usecases.c1.text
Corporate AI: The best ideas come from front-line staff who know where time is wasted. Workshops and process walkthroughs surface them quickly.

P.title: corp-usecases.c2.text
Corporate AI: Score each idea on business value and feasibility (data available, technical difficulty, risk). Start with high-value, high-feasibility ideas: quick wins.

P.title: corp-usecases.c3.text
Corporate AI: Is the data available and good enough? Can the output be checked? Is the process owner committed? Are there legal or regulatory constraints? Can it integrate with existing systems?

P.title: corp-usecases.c4.text
Corporate AI: Classify each use case by risk: internal drafting is low risk; decisions about people (hiring, credit) or safety are high risk and need stricter controls.

P.title: corp-usecases.c5.text
Corporate AI: Choose the right tool: generative AI for language and documents; predictive ML for numbers and forecasts; rules for simple deterministic logic. Many solutions combine them.

P.title: corp-usecases.c6.text
Corporate AI: Copilots assist a person (drafting, suggesting), keeping humans in control. Automation completes tasks end-to-end. Copilots are easier to adopt first; automation delivers bigger savings once trusted.

P.title: corp-usecases.c7.text
Corporate AI: Balance a portfolio: a few quick wins to build momentum, some larger transformational bets, and enabling foundations (data, platform, skills).

P.title: corp-usecases.c8.text
Corporate AI: For each use case: problem, users, expected value, data needed, success metric, risks, owner. A one-pager forces clarity before spending money.

P.title: corp-usecases.c9.text
Corporate AI: Not every idea works. Set a short timebox and clear success criteria for experiments, and stop those that don't meet them. Learning quickly is the goal.

P.title: corp-build.summary
Corporate AI: Choosing how to get AI capabilities.

P.title: corp-build.q0.q
Corporate AI: When does building usually make sense?

P.title: corp-build.q0.o1
Corporate AI: For core, differentiating processes with proprietary data

P.title: corp-build.q1.o1
Corporate AI: Abstraction layers, open standards and owning your data

P.title: corp-build.q2.q
Corporate AI: Before building a new AI tool you should check…

P.title: corp-build.q2.o1
Corporate AI: What AI features your existing software already offers

P.title: corp-build.q2.x
Corporate AI: Embedded AI may already cover it.

P.title: corp-build.c0.text
Corporate AI: Buy: use AI features in software you already have or SaaS tools. Build: develop your own solutions on models and platforms. Partner: work with a specialist or integrator.

P.title: corp-build.c1.text
Corporate AI: Buy for common needs where you don't differentiate: email drafting, meeting notes, generic chat, standard HR or CRM features. Faster and cheaper to start.

P.title: corp-build.c2.text
Corporate AI: Build where AI touches your competitive advantage or proprietary data, where integration with core systems is deep, or where off-the-shelf tools don't fit your process.

P.title: corp-build.c3.text
Corporate AI: ERP, CRM and productivity suites increasingly include AI (Microsoft Copilot, SAP Joule, Salesforce Einstein). Check what you already license before building.

P.title: corp-build.c4.text
Corporate AI: Building each use case from scratch is slow. A shared AI platform (model access, RAG, guardrails, monitoring) lets teams build many solutions faster and consistently.

P.title: corp-build.c5.text
Corporate AI: Relying on one model or vendor can be risky as the market moves fast. Abstraction layers, open standards and portable data reduce lock-in.

P.title: corp-build.c6.text
Corporate AI: Ask for evidence on your data: accuracy, security certifications, data handling terms, integration options, pricing at scale and roadmap.

P.title: corp-build.c7.text
Corporate AI: Count more than licences: integration, data preparation, change management, monitoring, support and model usage costs over several years.

P.title: corp-build.c8.text
Corporate AI: System integrators and specialist firms bring experience and capacity. Keep core knowledge in-house so you aren't dependent on them for every change.

P.title: corp-build.c9.text
Corporate AI: What you build today may become a commodity product next year. Review build/buy decisions as the market matures.

P.title: corp-roi.q0.q
Corporate AI: 10,000 items, 0.2 h saved each, €50/h, 50% adoption gives about…

P.title: corp-roi.q1.x
Corporate AI: Without it, gains can't be shown.

P.title: corp-roi.q2.q
Corporate AI: Saved time becomes real value when…

P.title: corp-roi.q2.o1
Corporate AI: It's redeployed to valuable work or reduces costs

P.title: corp-roi.c0.text
Corporate AI: Measure the current process first: time per task, volume, error rate, cost, cycle time. Without a baseline you can't prove improvement.

P.title: corp-roi.c1.text
Corporate AI: A simple estimate: volume × time saved per item × cost per hour × adoption rate. Be conservative.

P.title: corp-roi.c1.viz.f
Corporate AI: value = volume × time saved × hourly cost × adoption

P.title: corp-roi.c2.text
Corporate AI: Include quality improvements (fewer errors), faster cycle times (cash collected sooner), risk reduction and better decisions. These are often worth more than hours saved.

P.title: corp-roi.c3.text
Corporate AI: Include build costs, licences or model usage, integration, data preparation, change management, training and running costs for several years.

P.title: corp-roi.c4.text
Corporate AI: ROI compares net gain with cost; payback is how long until cumulative value covers investment.

P.title: corp-roi.c5.text
Corporate AI: A tool nobody uses delivers nothing. Model value with realistic adoption curves, rising over months, not 100% from day one.

P.title: corp-roi.c6.text
Corporate AI: Saved hours only become value if they're redeployed: more volume handled, better service, new work, or reduced overtime and outsourcing.

P.title: corp-roi.c7.text
Corporate AI: AI outcomes are uncertain. Present low, expected and high scenarios, and the assumptions behind each.

P.title: corp-roi.c8.text
Corporate AI: Track the same metrics as the baseline after launch and compare. Report real results, including what didn't work.

P.title: corp-roi.c9.text
Corporate AI: Some investments, such as data platforms or AI skills, don't pay back on one use case but enable many. Fund them as foundations, with a portfolio view.

P.title: corp-data.q0.q
Corporate AI: What is often the hardest part of corporate AI?

P.title: corp-data.q0.o1
Corporate AI: Finding, accessing and cleaning the right data

P.title: corp-data.q1.o1
Corporate AI: The single trusted version of core entities like customers and products

P.title: corp-data.q2.o1
Corporate AI: So access rules can be enforced, including for AI tools

P.title: corp-data.q2.x
Corporate AI: Users and AI should see only what's allowed.

P.title: corp-data.c0.text
Corporate AI: For most companies, the hardest part of AI is not the model but finding, accessing, cleaning and connecting the right data.

P.title: corp-data.c1.text
Corporate AI: A data catalogue lists what data exists, where it lives, who owns it, what it means and how sensitive it is. Without one, teams waste weeks searching.

P.title: corp-data.c2.text
Corporate AI: Quality means accuracy, completeness, consistency, timeliness and uniqueness. A dashboard of quality scores per key dataset makes problems visible.

P.title: corp-data.c3.text
Corporate AI: Customers, suppliers, products and materials should have one trusted version across systems. Messy master data breaks analytics and AI alike.

P.title: corp-data.c3.viz.items.0.w
Corporate AI: Bunge Ltd, "BUNGE", "Bunge S.A." as three suppliers

P.title: corp-data.c4.text
Corporate AI: Contracts, emails, PDFs and manuals hold huge value for generative AI but are often scattered across drives and mailboxes, with duplicates and outdated versions.

P.title: corp-data.c5.text
Corporate AI: Modern platforms (data lakehouses such as Databricks, Microsoft Fabric or Snowflake) bring data from many systems into one governed place for analytics and AI.

P.title: corp-data.c6.text
Corporate AI: Each important dataset needs a business owner accountable for its quality and access rules, supported by data stewards.

P.title: corp-data.c7.text
Corporate AI: Treat key datasets as products: documented, quality-checked, with clear owners and service levels, so many teams can reuse them reliably.

P.title: corp-data.c8.text
Corporate AI: Lineage shows where data came from and how it was transformed. It's essential for trusting AI outputs and for audits.

P.title: corp-data.c9.text
Corporate AI: Classify data (public, internal, confidential, restricted) and enforce access rules, so AI tools only see what each user is allowed to see.

P.title: corp-arch.summary
Corporate AI: The building blocks of an AI platform.

P.title: corp-arch.q0.q
Corporate AI: What does an AI gateway provide?

P.title: corp-arch.q0.o1
Corporate AI: Central routing, auth, logging, quotas and cost tracking

P.title: corp-arch.q0.x
Corporate AI: A control point between apps and models.

P.title: corp-arch.q1.q
Corporate AI: How should agents access ERP or CRM?

P.title: corp-arch.q1.o1
Corporate AI: Through well-defined, least-privilege APIs or MCP servers

P.title: corp-arch.q2.o1
Corporate AI: Inputs and outputs for injection, sensitive data and policy violations

P.title: corp-arch.q2.x
Corporate AI: They filter before and after the model.

P.title: corp-arch.c0.text
Corporate AI: A typical enterprise AI platform has: data sources, a data layer, model access, an orchestration layer (RAG, agents), guardrails, and applications, with security and monitoring across all.

P.title: corp-arch.c1.text
Corporate AI: A central gateway sits between applications and models. It handles authentication, routing, quotas, logging, cost tracking and content filters, and lets you swap models centrally.

P.title: corp-arch.c1.viz.steps.1
Corporate AI: AI gateway: auth, routing, logging, quotas

P.title: corp-arch.c2.text
Corporate AI: Offer approved models through the gateway: a few general models of different sizes, embedding models, and specialised ones. Document which to use for what.

P.title: corp-arch.c3.text
Corporate AI: Shared RAG services index approved document collections with permissions, so every team doesn't rebuild search and chunking from scratch.

P.title: corp-arch.c4.text
Corporate AI: Agents and copilots need safe access to systems: ERP, CRM, ticketing. Expose well-defined APIs or MCP servers rather than broad database access.

P.title: corp-arch.c5.text
Corporate AI: Input and output filters check for prompt injection, sensitive data, toxic content and policy violations. Business rules validate outputs before they reach customers or systems.

P.title: corp-arch.c6.text
Corporate AI: Log prompts, responses, tool calls, latency, costs and user feedback (with privacy controls). Traces help debug failures; dashboards show usage and spend.

P.title: corp-arch.c7.text
Corporate AI: Separate development, test and production, with evaluation gates before promotion, just like other software.

P.title: corp-arch.c8.text
Corporate AI: Choose model hosting regions that satisfy data residency rules (for example EU data in EU regions) and contract terms that prohibit training on your data.

P.title: corp-arch.c8.viz.items.2
Corporate AI: Encryption at rest and in transit

P.title: corp-arch.c9.text
Corporate AI: Document a reference architecture and reusable templates so teams can launch new AI applications quickly within guardrails.

P.title: corp-security.summary
Corporate AI: New risks and how to manage them.

P.title: corp-security.q0.x
Corporate AI: Best countered with good approved tools.

P.title: corp-security.q1.q
Corporate AI: Which principle limits damage from a hijacked agent?

P.title: corp-security.q1.o1
Corporate AI: Least privilege with approvals for sensitive actions

P.title: corp-security.q2.q
Corporate AI: Which standard defines an AI management system?

P.title: corp-security.c0.text
Corporate AI: AI systems add new risks: prompt injection, data leakage through prompts or outputs, poisoned training or retrieval data, model abuse and insecure tool access.

P.title: corp-security.c1.text
Corporate AI: Malicious instructions hidden in emails, web pages or documents can make an AI assistant reveal data or take actions. It's considered a top risk for LLM applications (OWASP).

P.title: corp-security.c1.viz.steps.0
Corporate AI: Attacker hides instructions in a document

P.title: corp-security.c1.viz.steps.3
Corporate AI: Guardrails and limited permissions stop harm

P.title: corp-security.c2.text
Corporate AI: Sensitive data can leak if users paste it into unapproved tools, if RAG ignores permissions, or if outputs include confidential details. Controls: approved tools, permission-aware retrieval and output filters.

P.title: corp-security.c3.text
Corporate AI: Employees using unapproved AI tools ("shadow AI") is common when approved options are lacking. The best defence is providing good approved tools plus clear guidance.

P.title: corp-security.c4.text
Corporate AI: Give AI agents the minimum access needed, scoped tokens, rate limits and approval steps for sensitive actions. Treat them like a new employee with very limited rights.

P.title: corp-security.c5.text
Corporate AI: Models, libraries and plugins come from third parties. Vet sources, scan dependencies and pin versions, like any other software supply chain.

P.title: corp-security.c6.text
Corporate AI: Using personal data in AI requires a lawful basis, purpose limitation, minimisation and often a data protection impact assessment (DPIA). Involve the DPO early.

P.title: corp-security.c7.text
Corporate AI: Before launch, test AI apps adversarially: try injections, jailbreaks, data extraction and misuse. Fix issues and retest.

P.title: corp-security.c8.text
Corporate AI: Have a plan for AI incidents: harmful outputs, data exposure, agent mistakes. Be able to disable features quickly, investigate logs and notify as required.

P.title: corp-security.c9.text
Corporate AI: Use established guidance: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications, NIST AI Risk Management Framework, ISO/IEC 42001 for AI management systems, plus your existing ISO 27001 controls.

P.title: corp-governance.summary
Corporate AI: Policies, roles and the EU AI Act in practice.

P.title: corp-governance.q0.q
Corporate AI: What should an AI inventory record?

P.title: corp-governance.q0.o1
Corporate AI: Use case, owner, data, model, risk level and controls

P.title: corp-governance.q1.q
Corporate AI: Since February 2025, the EU AI Act requires deployers to ensure…

P.title: corp-governance.q1.o1
Corporate AI: Sufficient AI literacy among staff using AI

P.title: corp-governance.q2.q
Corporate AI: How should governance treat low-risk use cases?

P.title: corp-governance.q2.o1
Corporate AI: Give them a fast lane with light checks

P.title: corp-governance.c0.text
Corporate AI: Governance makes sure AI is used safely, legally and in line with company values, without slowing everything down. Good governance enables faster adoption by clarifying the rules.

P.title: corp-governance.c0.viz.l.items.0
Corporate AI: incidents, or slow approvals and shadow AI

P.title: corp-governance.c1.text
Corporate AI: A short policy covers approved tools, permitted data, human oversight, transparency, prohibited uses and how to request new use cases.

P.title: corp-governance.c1.viz.items.4
Corporate AI: How to propose new use cases

P.title: corp-governance.c2.text
Corporate AI: Keep a register of AI systems and use cases: purpose, owner, data used, model, risk level and controls. The EU AI Act effectively requires knowing what you deploy.

P.title: corp-governance.c3.text
Corporate AI: Low-risk uses get a light self-assessment; high-risk ones go through a full review with legal, security, privacy and business experts.

P.title: corp-governance.c4.title
Corporate AI: The EU AI Act for companies

P.title: corp-governance.c4.text
Corporate AI: Companies are usually "deployers" of AI. For high-risk systems they must use them as instructed, ensure human oversight, monitor operation, keep logs and inform affected people. Banned practices must be avoided entirely.

P.title: corp-governance.c5.text
Corporate AI: Since February 2025, the EU AI Act requires providers and deployers to take measures to ensure sufficient AI literacy among staff who operate or use AI systems.

P.title: corp-governance.c6.text
Corporate AI: Typical roles: an executive sponsor, an AI governance board, use-case owners, a central AI team, plus legal, privacy, security and risk functions.

P.title: corp-governance.c7.text
Corporate AI: Banks and other regulated firms already manage model risk: validation, documentation, performance monitoring. Extend these practices to AI and LLMs.

P.title: corp-governance.c8.text
Corporate AI: Many AI risks come through vendors. Contracts should cover data use, security, transparency, incident notification and compliance with laws like the AI Act.

P.title: corp-governance.c9.text
Corporate AI: Pre-approved patterns (approved tools, templates, low-risk categories) let most teams move fast, while scrutiny focuses on high-risk cases.

P.title: corp-responsible.q0.q
Corporate AI: Which is an acceptable explanation for an AI-assisted decision?

P.title: corp-responsible.q0.o1
Corporate AI: The team decided using an AI recommendation

P.title: corp-responsible.q0.x
Corporate AI: A human or team stays accountable.

P.title: corp-responsible.q2.q
Corporate AI: What should an AI system do when uncertain?

P.title: corp-responsible.c0.text
Corporate AI: Most responsible AI frameworks share principles: fairness, transparency, accountability, privacy, safety and reliability, and human oversight.

P.title: corp-responsible.c1.text
Corporate AI: Check that AI doesn't treat people unfairly based on protected characteristics or proxies. Test outcomes across groups for any use affecting people.

P.title: corp-responsible.c2.text
Corporate AI: People should know when AI is involved and, for important decisions, understand the main reasons. Internally, document how systems work and their limits.

P.title: corp-responsible.c3.text
Corporate AI: A named person or team is accountable for each AI system's outcomes. "The algorithm decided" is never an acceptable answer.

P.title: corp-responsible.c3.viz.items.0.r
Corporate AI: the credit team decided, using an AI recommendation

P.title: corp-responsible.c4.text
Corporate AI: Decide where humans must review: before action (human-in-the-loop), monitoring with the ability to intervene (human-on-the-loop), or periodic audits.

P.title: corp-responsible.c5.text
Corporate AI: AI systems should perform consistently within their intended scope, with tested limits and graceful handling when uncertain: escalate rather than guess.

P.title: corp-responsible.c6.text
Corporate AI: Responsible adoption considers people: communicate openly, involve employees, invest in reskilling, and redesign roles thoughtfully.

P.title: corp-responsible.c7.text
Corporate AI: AI uses energy and water. Choose efficient models, avoid unnecessary use of the largest models and prefer cloud regions powered by clean energy.

P.title: corp-responsible.c8.text
Corporate AI: Short documents describing a system's purpose, data, performance, limitations and intended use help users and reviewers understand it.

P.title: corp-responsible.c9.text
Corporate AI: Responsible AI isn't a brake; it builds the trust that lets customers, regulators and employees accept AI at scale.

P.title: corp-ops.q0.q
Corporate AI: What should happen before a new prompt version is released?

P.title: corp-ops.q1.o1
Corporate AI: Incoming data changing so model performance degrades

P.title: corp-ops.q2.q
Corporate AI: What lets you switch an AI feature off without redeploying?

P.title: corp-ops.c0.text
Corporate AI: Unlike traditional software, AI behaviour depends on data and models that change. Production AI needs continuous monitoring, retraining and evaluation.

P.title: corp-ops.c1.text
Corporate AI: MLOps applies DevOps practices to machine learning: version data and models, automate training pipelines, test before deployment and monitor in production.

P.title: corp-ops.c2.text
Corporate AI: For generative AI, the moving parts are prompts, retrieval indexes, tools, guardrails and model versions. All should be versioned, tested and monitored.

P.title: corp-ops.c3.text
Corporate AI: Every change (new prompt, new model, new data) runs through automated evals before release. If quality drops, the change doesn't ship.

P.title: corp-ops.c3.viz.steps.3
Corporate AI: Ship only if equal or better

P.title: corp-ops.c4.text
Corporate AI: Track accuracy proxies (user feedback, correction rates, escalation rates), drift in inputs, latency, errors and cost. Sample outputs for human review.

P.title: corp-ops.c5.text
Corporate AI: When incoming data changes (new products, new document formats, new markets), model performance can degrade silently. Drift detection alerts the team.

P.title: corp-ops.c6.text
Corporate AI: Keep the previous version ready. If a release causes problems, roll back quickly. Feature flags let you switch AI features off without redeploying.

P.title: corp-ops.c6.viz.steps.2
Corporate AI: Feature flag off or roll back

P.title: corp-ops.c7.text
Corporate AI: Generative AI costs scale with usage. Track spend per application and team, set budgets and alerts, and optimise prompts and model choice.

P.title: corp-ops.c8.text
Corporate AI: Corrections made by users are valuable training and evaluation data. Capture them systematically to improve prompts, retrieval and models.

P.title: corp-ops.c9.text
Corporate AI: A central platform team usually provides the tooling (pipelines, gateway, monitoring, eval frameworks) so product teams can focus on use cases.

P.title: corp-scale.q0.o1
Corporate AI: Many pilots that never reach production

P.title: corp-scale.q0.x
Corporate AI: Pilots stall without owners, integration and proof of value.

P.title: corp-scale.q1.q
Corporate AI: Where should an AI tool live for high adoption?

P.title: corp-scale.q1.o1
Corporate AI: Inside the workflow tools people already use

P.title: corp-scale.q2.q
Corporate AI: What should happen to low-confidence AI results?

P.title: corp-scale.c0.text
Corporate AI: Many organisations run dozens of AI pilots that impress in demos but never scale. Common causes: no clear owner, no integration plan, unproven value and unresolved risk questions.

P.title: corp-scale.c1.title
Corporate AI: Design for production from day one

P.title: corp-scale.c1.text
Corporate AI: Even in a pilot, use real data, real users, the target architecture and security controls. A demo on clean sample data proves little.

P.title: corp-scale.c2.text
Corporate AI: Agree measurable success criteria before starting: accuracy threshold, time saved, user satisfaction, cost per transaction.

P.title: corp-scale.c3.text
Corporate AI: Value appears when AI is inside the workflow: in the ERP screen, the email client, the ticketing tool, not in a separate chat window people forget to use.

P.title: corp-scale.c4.text
Corporate AI: Design for the cases the AI can't handle: low confidence routes to humans, with an easy way to correct and learn.

P.title: corp-scale.c5.text
Corporate AI: Expand gradually: one team, one region, one document type, then more. Each step reveals new edge cases and builds confidence.

P.title: corp-scale.c6.text
Corporate AI: After launch someone must own it: monitoring, support, improvements and costs. Without an owner, solutions decay.

P.title: corp-scale.c7.text
Corporate AI: Once one use case works, turn it into a reusable pattern (document extraction, knowledge assistant, triage) and apply it across similar processes.

P.title: corp-scale.c8.text
Corporate AI: Share measured results internally: hours saved, errors avoided, user stories. Visible wins build momentum and funding for the next wave.

P.title: corp-scale.c9.text
Corporate AI: Not every pilot should scale. A disciplined stop decision frees resources and is a sign of a healthy portfolio.

P.title: corp-change.q0.q
Corporate AI: Why do many AI tools see low usage?

P.title: corp-change.q0.o1
Corporate AI: People aren't supported to change how they work

P.title: corp-change.q1.q
Corporate AI: What is an AI champions network?

P.title: corp-change.q1.o1
Corporate AI: Early adopters who help and train colleagues

P.title: corp-change.q2.q
Corporate AI: What does the "A" at the start of ADKAR stand for?

P.title: corp-change.q2.x
Corporate AI: Awareness of why change is needed.

P.title: corp-change.c0.text
Corporate AI: AI projects fail more often because people don't adopt them than because the technology fails. Change management deserves real budget and attention.

P.title: corp-change.c1.text
Corporate AI: People worry about job security, being monitored and looking incompetent. Leaders should explain the purpose honestly and how roles will evolve.

P.title: corp-change.c2.text
Corporate AI: Enthusiastic early users in each team help colleagues, share tips and give feedback. Peer learning spreads faster than central training.

P.title: corp-change.c3.text
Corporate AI: Short, practical sessions with real tasks from people's own work beat generic presentations. Show before-and-after examples.

P.title: corp-change.c4.text
Corporate AI: Dropping AI into an unchanged process gives small gains. Rethinking steps, roles and approvals around AI unlocks bigger ones.

P.title: corp-change.c5.text
Corporate AI: When leaders visibly use AI tools themselves and talk about it, adoption rises. If they don't, teams conclude it isn't important.

P.title: corp-change.c6.text
Corporate AI: Track active users, frequency, use cases, satisfaction and impact. Low adoption in a team is a signal to investigate, not just push harder.

P.title: corp-change.c7.text
Corporate AI: Single sign-on, integration in existing tools, prompt libraries and templates remove friction. Every extra click costs adoption.

P.title: corp-change.c8.text
Corporate AI: Share success stories, run internal showcases or hackathons, and recognise people who find valuable new uses.

P.title: corp-change.c9.text
Corporate AI: A common change model: Awareness of why, Desire to take part, Knowledge of how, Ability to do it, Reinforcement to make it stick.

P.title: corp-skills.summary
Corporate AI: Who does what in an AI-enabled company.

P.title: corp-skills.q0.q
Corporate AI: What does an AI Centre of Excellence do?

P.title: corp-skills.q0.o1
Corporate AI: Sets standards, builds shared platforms and supports teams

P.title: corp-skills.q1.q
Corporate AI: In a hub-and-spoke model, spokes are…

P.title: corp-skills.q1.o1
Corporate AI: AI teams embedded in business units

P.title: corp-skills.q2.q
Corporate AI: Why are domain experts essential to AI projects?

P.title: corp-skills.q2.o1
Corporate AI: They define what good looks like and validate outputs

P.title: corp-skills.c0.text
Corporate AI: Everyone using AI needs basic literacy: what it can and can't do, how to prompt, how to check outputs and what data rules apply. The EU AI Act now requires it.

P.title: corp-skills.c0.viz.items.0
Corporate AI: What AI can and can't do

P.title: corp-skills.c1.text
Corporate AI: Building AI needs a mix: product owners, data engineers, ML/AI engineers, software engineers, designers, and domain experts, plus governance roles.

P.title: corp-skills.c2.text
Corporate AI: A central AI CoE sets standards, builds the platform, shares best practice and helps teams. It avoids duplication and inconsistent controls.

P.title: corp-skills.c3.text
Corporate AI: A common model: a central hub (platform, governance, expertise) plus spokes embedded in business units who know local processes and drive use cases.

P.title: corp-skills.c4.text
Corporate AI: Large companies often combine global platform teams with regional delivery hubs, balancing standards with local needs and time zones.

P.title: corp-skills.c5.text
Corporate AI: Existing developers can learn AI engineering quickly: APIs, RAG, evaluation, prompt design. Upskilling plus a few specialists often beats hiring only new experts.

P.title: corp-skills.c6.text
Corporate AI: Accountants, traders, lawyers and engineers define what "good" looks like, label examples and validate outputs. Without them, AI solutions miss the point.

P.title: corp-skills.c7.text
Corporate AI: New roles are emerging: AI product manager, AI engineer, evaluation specialist, AI governance lead, and agent operations.

P.title: corp-skills.c8.text
Corporate AI: As routine tasks shrink, roles shift toward judgement, exception handling, relationships and supervising AI. Clear career paths reduce anxiety and keep talent.

P.title: corp-skills.c9.text
Corporate AI: AI changes fast. Build learning into the job: communities of practice, internal demos, learning budgets and time to experiment.

P.title: corp-finance.title
Corporate AI: AI in finance and back office

P.title: corp-finance.q0.o1
Corporate AI: Matching PO, goods receipt and invoice

P.title: corp-finance.q1.q
Corporate AI: Why must finance AI keep an audit trail?

P.title: corp-finance.q1.o1
Corporate AI: So auditors can trace every posting to sources and approvals

P.title: corp-finance.q2.o1
Corporate AI: Share of items processed without human intervention

P.title: corp-finance.c0.text
Corporate AI: AI extracts supplier, dates, amounts, VAT and line items from invoices in any layout, matches them to purchase orders and goods receipts, and flags mismatches.

P.title: corp-finance.c1.text
Corporate AI: Classic accounts payable check: invoice, purchase order and goods receipt must agree on quantities and prices. AI speeds matching and explains mismatches.

P.title: corp-finance.c2.text
Corporate AI: Matching bank statements, intercompany balances and ledgers is repetitive. ML can match transactions with fuzzy references and learn from past manual matches.

P.title: corp-finance.c3.text
Corporate AI: AI can draft variance explanations, check journal entries for anomalies and summarise close status, shortening month-end.

P.title: corp-finance.c4.text
Corporate AI: ML models forecast customer payments and supplier outflows from history, improving cash and working-capital planning.

P.title: corp-finance.c5.text
Corporate AI: Detect duplicate invoices, unusual payments, changed bank details and suspicious vendors before money leaves.

P.title: corp-finance.c6.text
Corporate AI: AI reads receipts, checks them against policy and flags exceptions, so auditors review the risky few instead of sampling randomly.

P.title: corp-finance.c7.text
Corporate AI: Finance needs full traceability: every AI-proposed posting should show source documents, confidence and who approved it. Auditors must be able to follow the trail.

P.title: corp-finance.c8.text
Corporate AI: Value comes when AI is connected to the ERP (SAP S/4HANA, Oracle, Dynamics): reading master data, proposing postings, updating workflows.

P.title: corp-finance.c9.text
Corporate AI: Track touchless processing rate, cycle time, error rate, cost per invoice, days to close and early-payment discounts captured.

P.title: corp-supply.q1.q
Corporate AI: In trade contracts, what is demurrage?

P.title: corp-supply.q1.o1
Corporate AI: A charge per day when a vessel is delayed beyond agreed laytime

P.title: corp-supply.q2.q
Corporate AI: Who should make final trading decisions?

P.title: corp-supply.c0.text
Corporate AI: ML forecasts demand using history, seasonality, prices, weather and events, improving on simple averages and helping plan production and stock.

P.title: corp-supply.c1.text
Corporate AI: AI combines data from ERP, carriers, ports and suppliers to predict delays and suggest actions, such as rerouting or reprioritising orders.

P.title: corp-supply.c2.text
Corporate AI: Optimisation and ML plan routes, vessel schedules, warehouse picking and truck loading, reducing cost and emissions.

P.title: corp-supply.c3.text
Corporate AI: Sensors on machines (vibration, temperature, power) feed models that predict failures, so maintenance happens before breakdowns.

P.title: corp-supply.c4.text
Corporate AI: Models combine supply and demand data, weather, crop conditions, freight and macro indicators to support analysts' views. They inform, not replace, trading judgement.

P.title: corp-supply.c5.text
Corporate AI: Satellite images and weather forecasts help estimate crop health and yields across regions like Brazil, the US Midwest and the Black Sea before official reports.

P.title: corp-supply.c6.text
Corporate AI: Generative AI extracts key terms from trade contracts (quantities, quality specs, shipment periods, Incoterms, demurrage, payment terms) and flags unusual clauses.

P.title: corp-supply.c7.text
Corporate AI: AI helps with documents (bills of lading, certificates, letters of credit), checking consistency across them and spotting discrepancies before they cause payment delays.

P.title: corp-supply.c8.text
Corporate AI: Sanctions screening, counterparty risk and vessel tracking benefit from AI that monitors news, ownership data and ship movements.

P.title: corp-supply.c9.text
Corporate AI: In trading and operations, AI provides signals and automation, while experienced people make the commercial and risk decisions.

P.title: corp-customer.title
Corporate AI: AI in customer service and sales

P.title: corp-customer.q0.q
Corporate AI: What does a support copilot do?

P.title: corp-customer.q0.o1
Corporate AI: Drafts replies for agents to review and send

P.title: corp-customer.q1.q
Corporate AI: What must a customer-facing assistant offer?

P.title: corp-customer.q1.o1
Corporate AI: A way to reach a human

P.title: corp-customer.c0.text
Corporate AI: AI drafts replies for agents using knowledge bases and case history. Agents edit and send, handling more cases with consistent quality.

P.title: corp-customer.c1.text
Corporate AI: Customer-facing assistants answer common questions 24/7 and hand over to humans for complex or sensitive cases, with full context passed on.

P.title: corp-customer.c2.text
Corporate AI: Classify incoming requests by topic, urgency and language, and route them to the right team automatically.

P.title: corp-customer.c3.text
Corporate AI: AI analyses conversations for sentiment, recurring issues and compliance, giving managers insight across all interactions, not just samples.

P.title: corp-customer.c4.text
Corporate AI: AI prepares account briefings, summarises meetings, drafts proposals and updates the CRM, giving salespeople more time with customers.

P.title: corp-customer.c5.text
Corporate AI: ML scores leads by likelihood to buy, based on past wins, behaviour and firmographics, so sales focuses on the most promising.

P.title: corp-customer.c6.text
Corporate AI: Models suggest prices or discounts based on deal history, demand and competition, within guardrails set by the business.

P.title: corp-customer.c7.text
Corporate AI: Recommending relevant products and content increases conversion, but must respect privacy and avoid being intrusive.

P.title: corp-customer.c8.text
Corporate AI: Customers should know when they're talking to AI, and should always be able to reach a human. The EU AI Act requires disclosure for chatbots.

P.title: corp-customer.c9.text
Corporate AI: Track resolution rate, handling time, customer satisfaction, escalation rate and accuracy of answers. Watch for customers giving up.

P.title: corp-hrlegal.q0.q
Corporate AI: Under the EU AI Act, AI that ranks job candidates is…

P.title: corp-hrlegal.q1.q
Corporate AI: What does a legal playbook define?

P.title: corp-hrlegal.q1.o1
Corporate AI: Preferred, acceptable and unacceptable clause positions

P.title: corp-hrlegal.q2.q
Corporate AI: Which practice is banned at work under the EU AI Act?

P.title: corp-hrlegal.c0.text
Corporate AI: AI extracts key clauses (term, renewal, liability, termination, governing law), compares them with your standard positions and highlights deviations for lawyers.

P.title: corp-hrlegal.c1.text
Corporate AI: A legal playbook defines preferred, acceptable and unacceptable positions for each clause. AI applies it consistently across thousands of contracts.

P.title: corp-hrlegal.c2.text
Corporate AI: AI helps search case law and regulations, but citations must be verified: lawyers have been sanctioned for submitting AI-invented cases.

P.title: corp-hrlegal.c3.text
Corporate AI: Employees ask questions about HR policies, travel rules or IT procedures and get answers grounded in official documents, with links.

P.title: corp-hrlegal.c4.text
Corporate AI: CV screening and candidate ranking are high-risk under the EU AI Act. Use AI to assist (writing job ads, scheduling, summarising), and keep humans making decisions, with bias testing.

P.title: corp-hrlegal.c5.text
Corporate AI: AI assistants guide new employees through systems, policies and first tasks, answering questions any time.

P.title: corp-hrlegal.c6.text
Corporate AI: AI creates learning content, quizzes and personalised paths, and acts as a tutor, like this app.

P.title: corp-hrlegal.c7.text
Corporate AI: HR data is sensitive. Restrict access, minimise data, avoid emotion recognition at work (banned under the EU AI Act) and involve works councils where required.

P.title: corp-hrlegal.c8.text
Corporate AI: AI tracks regulatory changes, maps them to internal policies and flags gaps, helping compliance teams keep up.

P.title: corp-hrlegal.c9.text
Corporate AI: AI speeds legal work, but professional responsibility stays with lawyers. Use it for first drafts, review and research support, with expert sign-off.

P.title: corp-dev.q0.q
Corporate AI: What should happen to AI-generated code before merging?

P.title: corp-dev.q0.o1
Corporate AI: Human review, tests and security scanning

P.title: corp-dev.q1.o1
Corporate AI: AI suggesting a non-existent library name that attackers could register

P.title: corp-dev.q2.q
Corporate AI: Which is a good measure of AI's engineering impact?

P.title: corp-dev.q2.o1
Corporate AI: Cycle time and change failure rate

P.title: corp-dev.c0.text
Corporate AI: Tools like GitHub Copilot, Cursor and Claude Code suggest code, explain it, write tests and fix bugs, inside the developer's editor or terminal.

P.title: corp-dev.c1.text
Corporate AI: Controlled studies have found developers complete some coding tasks substantially faster with AI assistants, though gains vary by task, experience and codebase.

P.title: corp-dev.c2.text
Corporate AI: Agents take a task (an issue or ticket), plan changes across files, run tests and open a pull request for human review.

P.title: corp-dev.c3.text
Corporate AI: AI-generated code can contain bugs, security issues or licence problems. Keep code review, tests and security scanning in the pipeline.

P.title: corp-dev.c4.text
Corporate AI: AI helps understand and document legacy code (COBOL, old ABAP), suggest migrations and generate tests, speeding up modernisation projects like S/4HANA moves.

P.title: corp-dev.c5.text
Corporate AI: AI writes and updates documentation, API descriptions and runbooks from code and commit history, reducing a chore developers often skip.

P.title: corp-dev.c6.text
Corporate AI: AI generates unit tests, test data and edge cases, raising coverage quickly. Developers still check the tests actually test the right thing.

P.title: corp-dev.c7.text
Corporate AI: AI makes it easier for non-developers to build automations and small apps, but governance is needed for security, data access and maintenance.

P.title: corp-dev.c8.text
Corporate AI: Watch for hard-coded secrets, injection flaws, outdated libraries and hallucinated package names that attackers might register.

P.title: corp-dev.c9.text
Corporate AI: Track cycle time, deployment frequency, change failure rate, developer satisfaction and time spent on toil, not lines of code generated.

P.title: corp-value.q1.o1
Corporate AI: To separate AI's effect from other changes

P.title: corp-value.q2.q
Corporate AI: What is a leading indicator of AI value?

P.title: corp-value.c0.text
Corporate AI: Count outcomes (cost saved, revenue gained, errors avoided, time to serve customers), not activity (number of prompts, pilots launched, users invited).

P.title: corp-value.c1.text
Corporate AI: Track usage (are people using it?), performance (is it accurate and fast?) and business impact (is it creating value?).

P.title: corp-value.c2.text
Corporate AI: Time per task, throughput per person, touchless rates, backlog size and cycle times show productivity effects.

P.title: corp-value.c3.text
Corporate AI: Error rates, rework, compliance findings and customer complaints show whether AI improves or harms quality.

P.title: corp-value.c4.text
Corporate AI: Translate gains into money: cost avoided, revenue uplift, working capital released, risk losses avoided, and compare with full costs.

P.title: corp-value.c5.text
Corporate AI: Where possible, compare teams or periods with and without AI. Otherwise improvements may be due to other changes.

P.title: corp-value.c6.text
Corporate AI: A shared AI value dashboard shows each use case's adoption, quality and value against targets, building transparency for leadership.

P.title: corp-value.c7.text
Corporate AI: Value often lags. Early signals like adoption, satisfaction and reduced handling time predict later financial results.

P.title: corp-value.c8.text
Corporate AI: Report what didn't work, not just successes. Credibility with finance and leadership comes from realistic numbers.

P.title: corp-value.c9.text
Corporate AI: Manage AI as a portfolio: some use cases deliver big wins, many modest gains, some fail. The total portfolio return is what matters.

P.title: corp-strategy.q0.q
Corporate AI: What should an AI strategy serve?

P.title: corp-strategy.q0.x
Corporate AI: AI is a means, not the end.

P.title: corp-strategy.q1.q
Corporate AI: When should foundations (data, platform, governance) be built?

P.title: corp-strategy.q2.q
Corporate AI: How often should the AI strategy be revisited?

P.title: corp-strategy.c0.text
Corporate AI: An AI strategy should serve the company strategy: growth, efficiency, risk, customer experience. Each AI initiative links to a business goal.

P.title: corp-strategy.c1.text
Corporate AI: Companies range from experimenting, to scaling selected use cases, to transforming core processes and business models with AI.

P.title: corp-strategy.c2.text
Corporate AI: A roadmap sequences use cases and foundations over 12–36 months, with waves: quick wins first, foundations in parallel, bigger transformations later.

P.title: corp-strategy.c3.text
Corporate AI: Data, platform, governance, security and skills must be built alongside use cases, not after. Each wave of use cases funds and uses the foundations.

P.title: corp-strategy.c4.text
Corporate AI: Decide who funds, builds, owns and governs AI: central, federated or hybrid. Hybrid hub-and-spoke is common in large global companies.

P.title: corp-strategy.c5.text
Corporate AI: Strategic partners (cloud providers, model providers, integrators, startups) speed delivery. Keep architecture and key skills in-house.

P.title: corp-strategy.c6.text
Corporate AI: Fund foundations centrally, use cases by business units (with central co-funding to start), and review the portfolio quarterly.

P.title: corp-strategy.c7.text
Corporate AI: As agents mature, more end-to-end processes may be automated with human oversight. Prepare now: clean APIs, clear processes, good data and governance for autonomous actions.

P.title: corp-strategy.c8.text
Corporate AI: Models, prices and regulations change quickly. Revisit the strategy at least yearly, keep architecture flexible and avoid betting everything on one vendor.

P.title: corp-strategy.c9.text
Corporate AI: The companies that win with AI combine technology with people who know the business, trust built through responsible practices, and a culture of learning.
